canonical_name: MiniSom -- a minimal Self-Organizing Map in Python (Giuseppe Vettigli)
lineage: The Self-Organizing Map (Kohonen 1982): an unsupervised connectionist network whose neurons arrange on a grid and adapt so that nearby neurons respond to similar inputs -- competitive learning that forms a topology-preserving map of the data
version: github.com/JustGlowing/minisom master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

example.command: Techne harness: train a small SOM on clustered 2-D points, check the quantization error drops and nearby cells map nearby clusters
example.output: a trained map; quantization error decreasing over training

upstream_docs: Kohonen, Self-Organized Formation of Topologically Correct Feature Maps, 1982

human_capability_summary.built_to: learn, without labels, a low-dimensional (grid) representation of high-dimensional data where neighbouring grid cells respond to similar inputs -- competitive, neighbourhood-cooperative weight adaptation
human_capability_summary.pressure: unlabelled high-dimensional data with unknown structure; the map must discover clusters and topology by competition alone
human_capability_summary.success_means: a topology-preserving map: similar inputs excite nearby neurons, and quantization error falls as it self-organises

human_environmental_pressure: unlabelled, high-dimensional data; no supervisory signal
human_failure_condition: a bad learning rate/neighbourhood schedule leaves the map twisted or collapsed -- it fails to separate the clusters
behavioral_entry_point: shrink the neighbourhood radius or learning-rate schedule, or feed non-clustered noise, and watch the map fail to organise

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run minisom
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: learn, without labels, a low-dimensional (grid) representation of high-dimensional data where neighbouring grid cells respond to similar inputs -- competitive, neighbourhood-cooperative weight adaptation
